claims.claim: DeBERTa disentangled attention uses content-to-content, content-to-position and position-to-content score terms, removing position-to-position in the principal implementation.
claims.verification_note: Three-term rather than four-term default is important.

claims.claim: Position-to-content term uses reverse relative-distance index delta(j,i), while content-to-position uses delta(i,j).
claims.verification_note: Direction reversal is an explicit claim in the paper.

claims.claim: Original paper three-term attention normalizes scores by square root of 3d.
claims.verification_note: Implementation may adjust scale with enabled term count.

claims.claim: Enhanced Mask Decoder incorporates absolute positions in the MLM decoding stage rather than being a generative sequence-to-sequence decoder.
claims.verification_note: Original model is an encoder for language understanding.

claims.claim: Microsoft reference implementation has configurable c2p, p2c and optional p2p score branches.
claims.verification_note: Versioned code options are distinguished from default original paper equation.

claims.claim: Original DeBERTa dense attention still computes token-pair T by T scores.
claims.verification_note: Relative position embeddings do not imply sparse attention or eliminate quadratic pairwise interactions.
